title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
description: Animated KS3 Maths lesson on fractions, decimals and percentages for ages 9 to 14: what fractions mean, equivalent fractions and simplifying, converting between fractions, decimals and percentages, adding, subtracting and multiplying fractions, and finding fractions and percentages of amounts.
intro: Three ways to write the same amount: {1/2}, 0.5 and 50%. Equivalent fractions, converting, calculating and parts of amounts, explained by the owl in five short parts.

steps.say: A fraction is part of a whole. The **bottom number** says how many **equal parts** there are. The **top number** says how many we have.
This pizza has 8 equal slices and 3 are shaded, so {3/8} of it is shaded.
steps.speak: This pizza has 8 equal slices and 3 are shaded, so three eighths of it is shaded.

steps.say: Fractions live on the number line too. Split 0 to 1 into 5 equal steps. The arrow points at {3/5}.
steps.speak: Fractions live on the number line too. Split 0 to 1 into 5 equal steps. The arrow points at three fifths.

steps.say: Bars of the same length help you compare. {2/3} covers more than {3/5}, so {2/3} is bigger.
steps.speak: Bars of the same length help you compare. Two thirds covers more than three fifths, so two thirds is bigger.

check.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. 5 slices are eaten. What fraction is eaten?
check.hint: The bottom number is how many equal slices there are altogether.
check.explain: There are 8 equal slices and 5 are eaten, so **{5/8}** is eaten.

steps.say: {1/2}, {2/4} and {4/8} look different, but they cover **the same amount**. They are **equivalent** fractions.
steps.speak: One half, two quarters and four eighths look different, but they cover the same amount. They are equivalent fractions.

steps.say: To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by **the same number**. {2/5} = {8/20}, because both were multiplied by 4.
steps.speak: To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. Two fifths equals eight twentieths, because both were multiplied by 4.

steps.say: To **simplify**, divide the top and the bottom by the same number. {18/24}: divide both by 6 to get {3/4}.
steps.speak: To simplify, divide the top and the bottom by the same number. Eighteen twenty-fourths: divide both by 6 to get three quarters.

steps.say: A fraction is in its **simplest form** when no number except 1 divides into both the top and the bottom.

check.hint: Find the biggest number that divides into both 12 and 16.
check.explain: 4 divides into both: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so {12/16} = **{3/4}**. ({6/8} is equal, but it can still be simplified.)

steps.say: **Per cent** means 'out of 100'. Here 25 squares out of 100 are coloured, so that is **25%**.
steps.speak: Per cent means out of 100. Here 25 squares out of 100 are coloured, so that is 25 per cent.

steps.say: {1/2}, 0.5 and 50% are three ways to write **the same amount**.
steps.speak: One half, nought point 5, and 50 per cent are three ways to write the same amount.

steps.say: To change a fraction to a percentage, make the bottom 100. {3/5} = {60/100} = 60%, which is 0.6 as a decimal.
steps.speak: To change a fraction to a percentage, make the bottom 100. Three fifths equals sixty hundredths, which is 60 per cent, or nought point 6 as a decimal.

These are worth learning: one quarter is nought point 2 5, which is 25 per cent. Three quarters is nought point 7 5, which is 75 per cent. One tenth is nought point 1, which is 10 per cent. And one fifth is nought point 2, which is 20 per cent.

check.hint: To change a decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100.
check.explain: 0.4 × 100 = 40, so 0.4 = **40%**. (0.4 is 4 tenths, which is 40 hundredths.)

steps.say: When the bottom numbers are the same, add the tops: {2/7} + {3/7} = {5/7}. The bottom stays the same.
steps.speak: When the bottom numbers are the same, add the tops: two sevenths plus three sevenths equals five sevenths. The bottom stays the same.

steps.say: When the bottoms are different, make them the same first: {1/2} + {1/4} = {2/4} + {1/4} = {3/4}.
steps.speak: When the bottoms are different, make them the same first: one half plus one quarter equals two quarters plus one quarter, which equals three quarters.
Two thirds minus one quarter: twelfths work for both. Eight twelfths minus three twelfths equals five twelfths.

steps.say: To multiply, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms. {3/4} × {2/5} = {6/20}, which simplifies to {3/10}.
steps.speak: To multiply, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms. Three quarters times two fifths equals six twentieths, which simplifies to three tenths.

steps.say: To find {3/4} of 20, **divide by the bottom**, then **times by the top**. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, and 5 × 3 = 15.
steps.speak: To find three quarters of 20, divide by the bottom, then times by the top. 20 divided by 4 equals 5, and 5 times 3 equals 15.
50 per cent is a half, so 50 per cent of 36 equals 36 divided by 2, which equals 18.

steps.say: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10. 10% of £45 = **£4.50**.
steps.speak: 10 per cent is a tenth, so divide by 10. 10 per cent of 45 pounds equals 4 pounds 50.

steps.say: Build other percentages from 10%. 30% is 3 lots of 10%: 3 × £4.50 = **£13.50**. And 25% is a quarter: 25% of 80 kg = **20 kg**.
steps.speak: Build other percentages from 10 per cent. 30 per cent is 3 lots of 10 per cent: 3 times 4 pounds 50 equals 13 pounds 50. And 25 per cent is a quarter: 25 per cent of 80 kilograms equals 20 kilograms.
